en: The Bible never says Noah's Ark landed on Mount Ararat.
Not once.
Genesis says only this.
The Ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.
Mountains, plural.
And Ararat wasn't a peak.
It was a kingdom.
Uratu, around Lake Van.
So where did it really stop?
The oldest Jewish translation of Genesis, the Targum Onkelos, gives a different name.
Not Ararat.
Cardu, nearly 300 years before Christ, a Babylonian priest named Erosus, wrote
that pieces of the ship could still be found.
In the Gordian Mountains, then the Qur'an names a single peak.
Al-Judy, Cardu, Gordian, Judi.
Three names, and many scholars trace all three to the same corner of southeastern
Turkey.
Mount Qudi, not even half the height of Ararat, the giant volcano we now call Mount
Ararat, only took the title centuries later.
So, Ararat or Qudi?
Or do you think Noah's Ark really existed?
Tell me in the comments.
